arxiv-2103-04361.title: Detection of bistable structures via the Conley index and applications to biological systems
arxiv-2103-04361.creator: Junbo Jia, Pan Yang, Huaiping Zhu, Zhen Jin, Jinqiao Duan, Xinchu Fu
arxiv-2103-04361.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Junbo Jia, Pan Yang, Huaiping Zhu, Zhen Jin, Jinqiao Duan, Xinchu Fu. Bistability is a ubiquitous phenomenon in life sciences. In this paper, two kinds of bistable structures in dynamical systems are studied: One is two one-point attractors, another is a one-point attractor accompanied by a cycle attractor. By the Conley index theory, we prove that there exist other isolated invariant sets besides the two attractors, and also obtain the possible components and their configuration.

arxiv-2107-03856.title: Characterization of biophysical determinants of spatio-temporal calcium dynamics in astrocytes
arxiv-2107-03856.creator: Thais Appelt Peres Bartiê, Leonel Teixeira Pinto
arxiv-2107-03856.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Thais Appelt Peres Bartiê, Leonel Teixeira Pinto. Most of the functions performed by astrocytes in brain information processing are related to calcium waves. Experimental studies involving calcium waves present discrepant results, leading to gaps in the full understanding of the functions of these cells. The use of mathematical models help to understand the experimental results, identifying chemical mechanisms involved in calcium waves and the limits of experimental methods. The model is diffusion-based and uses receptors and channels as boundary conditions.

arxiv-2208-06648.title: Imputation Strategies Under Clinical Presence: Impact on Algorithmic Fairness
arxiv-2208-06648.creator: Vincent JeanselmeMRC Biostatistics UnitUniversity of Cambridge, UKThe Alan Turing Institute vincent.jeanselme@mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk Maria De-ArteagaMcCombs School of BusinessUniversity of Texas at Austin, USA, Zhe ZhangRady School of ManagementUniversity of California, San Diego, USAJessica BarrettMRC B
arxiv-2208-06648.description: Abstract Machine learning risks reinforcing biases present in data and, as we argue in this work, in what is absent from data. In healthcare, societal and decision biases shape patterns in missing data, yet the algorithmic fairness implications of group-specific missingness are poorly understood. The way we address missingness in healthcare can have detrimental impacts on downstream algorithmic fairness.

arxiv-2304-01903.title: Eco-evolutionary dynamics in finite network-structured populations with migration
arxiv-2304-01903.description: Abstract We consider the effect of network structure on the evolution of a population. Models of this kind typically consider a population of fixed size and distribution. Here we consider eco-evolutionary dynamics where population size and distribution can change through birth, death and migration, all of which are separate processes.

arxiv-2310-12665.title: SecurityNet : Assessing Machine Learning Vulnerabilities on Public Models
arxiv-2310-12665.creator: Boyang Zhang Zheng Li Ziqing Yang Xinlei He Michael Backes Mario Fritz Yang Zhang
arxiv-2310-12665.description: Abstract While advanced machine learning (ML) models are deployed in numerous real-world applications, previous works demonstrate these models have security and privacy vulnerabilities. Various empirical research has been done in this field. However, most of the experiments are performed on target ML models trained by the security researchers themselves.

arxiv-2312-10799.title: Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz over quaternions
arxiv-2312-10799.creator: Masood Aryapoor
arxiv-2312-10799.description: Abstract Using the Rabinowitsch trick, we prove a version of Nullstellensatz over quaternions, which generalizes Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz over complex numbers. 1 Introduction In [ 1 ] , two forms of (central) Nullstellensatz over the division ring of quaternions \mathbb{H} are presented: a weak form and a strong form.

arxiv-2402-12461.title: Fossil Signatures of Main-sequence Convective Core Overshoot Estimated through Asteroseismic Analyses MESA ( Paxton et al. 2011 ; Paxton et al. 2013 ; Paxton et al. 2015 ; Paxton et al. 2018 ; Paxton et al. 2019 ; Jermyn et al. 2023 ) , GYRE ( Townsend & Teitler 2013 )
arxiv-2402-12461.creator: Christopher J. Lindsay, J. M. Joel Ong, Sarbani Basu
arxiv-2402-12461.description: Abstract Some physical processes that occur during a star’s main-sequence evolution also affect its post main-sequence evolution. It is well known that stars with masses above approximately 1.1 M ⊙ M_{\odot} have well-mixed convective cores on the main sequence, however, the structure of the star in the neighborhood of the convective core regions is currently underconstrained.

arxiv-2404-01984.title: Fashion Style Editing with Generative Human Prior
arxiv-2404-01984.creator: Chaerin Kong, Seungyong Lee, Soohyeok Im, Wonsuk YangNXN Labs {chaerin,seungyong,soohyeok,wonsuk}@nxn.ai
arxiv-2404-01984.description: Abstract Image editing has been a long-standing challenge in the research community with its far-reaching impact on numerous applications. Recently, text-driven methods started to deliver promising results in domains like human faces, but their applications to more complex domains have been relatively limited.

arxiv-2405-13887.title: Multi-Zone Modeling of Black Hole Accretion and Feedback in 3D GRMHD: Bridging Vast Spatial and Temporal Scales
arxiv-2405-13887.creator: Hyerin Cho (조혜린), Ben S. Prather, Kung-Yi Su, Ramesh Narayan, Priyamvada Natarajan
arxiv-2405-13887.description: Abstract Simulating accretion and feedback from the horizon scale of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) out to galactic scales is challenging because of the vast range of scales involved. Elaborating on Cho et al. 2023 , we describe and test a “multi-zone” technique which is designed to tackle this difficult problem in 3D general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations.

arxiv-2507-21889.title: When is the diagonal contractible?
arxiv-2507-21889.creator: Xi Chen, Frank Gounelas
arxiv-2507-21889.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xi Chen, Frank Gounelas. For a smooth projective complex variety X X , we prove that there exists a birational morphism X × X → Y X\times X\to Y to a projective variety Y Y contracting the diagonal Δ X ⊂ X × X \Delta_{X}\subset X\times X to a point if and only if X X has maximal Albanese dimension and irregularity q ≥ 2 ​ dim X q\geq 2\dim X .

arxiv-2508-13263.title: The New Status Qvo? SN 2021qvo is Another 2003fg-like Type Ia Supernova with a Rising Light-Curve Bump Facilities: Pan-STARRS astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , SNooPy ( Burns et al. 2011b )
arxiv-2508-13263.creator: I. A. Abreu Paniagua, W. B. Hoogendam, D. O. Jones, G. Dimitriadis, R. J. Foley, C. Gall, J. O’Brien, K. Taggart, C. R. Angus, C. Ashall, K. Auchettl, D. A. Coulter, K. W. Davis, T. de Boer, A. Do, H. Gao, L. Izzo, C.-C. Lin, T. B. Lowe, Z. Lai, R. Kaur, M. Y. Kong, A. Rest, M. R. Siebert, S. K. Yad
arxiv-2508-13263.description: Abstract In recent years, multiple Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) have been observed with “bumps” in their rising light curves shortly after explosion. Here, we present SN 2021qvo: a SN Ia that exhibits a clear early bump in photometry obtained by the Young Supernova Experiment.

arxiv-2508-15157.title: Big-Stop Semantics DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX CCS: Theory of computation Operational semantics CCS: Theory of computation Algebraic semantics
arxiv-2508-15157.creator: David M Kahn, Jan Hoffmann, Runming Li
arxiv-2508-15157.description: Abstract . As evident in the programming language literature, many practitioners favor specifying dynamic program behavior using big-step over small-step semantics. Unlike small-step semantics, which must dwell on every intermediate program state, big-step semantics conveniently jump directly to the ever-important result of the computation. Big-step semantics also typically involve fewer inference rules than their small-step counterparts.

arxiv-2509-08042.title: Testing the Heterotic String with the Axion-Photon Coupling
arxiv-2509-08042.creator: Mario Reig, and Timo Weigand
arxiv-2509-08042.description: Abstract The discovery of an axion-like particle above the QCD line would rule out Grand Unified Theories, including the perturbative heterotic string with the Standard Model embedded in a single E 8 E_{8} factor or S ​ O ​ ( 32 ) SO(32) .

arxiv-2512-02260.title: EcoCast: A Spatio-Temporal Model for Continual Biodiversity and Climate Risk Forecasting
arxiv-2512-02260.creator: Hammed A. Akande, Abdulrauf A. Gidado
arxiv-2512-02260.description: Abstract Increasing climate change and habitat loss are driving unprecedented shifts in species distributions. Conservation professionals urgently need timely, high-resolution predictions of biodiversity risks, especially in ecologically diverse regions like Africa. We propose EcoCast , a spatio-temporal model designed for continual biodiversity and climate risk forecasting.

marlowe-dido-1594.creator: Christopher Marlowe
marlowe-dido-1594.description: Dido's love and death — the classical tragedy of Marlowe's youth.

pmc-10594512.title: Assessment of the Brazilian Version of the Epworth Sleepiness Scale Using Item Response Theory: A Psychometric Study
pmc-10594512.creator: Cleber Lopes Campelo, Rosângela Fernandes Lucena Batista, Victor Nogueira da Cruz Silveira, Kely Nayara dos Reis Silva Figueiredo, Patrícia Maria Abreu Machado, Adriano Ferreti Borgatto, Alcione Miranda dos Santos, Tamar Shochat
pmc-10594512.description: There seems to be a consensus that adolescents worldwide are not getting enough sleep. This study aimed to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) in adolescents using the item response theory. A psychometric study was conducted with 2206 adolescents aged 18 and 19 years in the city of São Luís, Maranhão, Brazil.

pmc-10595560.title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on COPD patients: a nationwide mortality study in France
pmc-10595560.creator: J Poucineau, M Khlat, N Lapidus, M Espagnacq, C Chouaïd, T Delory, S Le Coeur
pmc-10595560.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) patients are a vulnerable population with an increased risk of death from COVID-19 if infected. To date, a reduction in hospitalizations for acute exacerbations of COPD has been reported in various contexts, but large population-based studies with mortality follow-up are lacking.

pmc-10728665.title: Does prior knowledge affect interaction dynamics and learning achievement in digital problem-based learning? A pilot study
pmc-10728665.creator: Martin Möser, Rico Hermkes, Natalie Filmann, Seon-Yee Harsch, Stefan Rüttermann, Susanne Gerhard-Szép
pmc-10728665.description: Objective: Previous research on problem-based learning (PBL) describes that videotaped observations develop meaningful insights into cognitive processes in tutorial groups. Analysis regarding the amount of prior knowledge on learning achievement has not been investigated in medical education so far, although both are key factors of PBL success.

pmc-12532846.title: Distinct inflammatory profiles across migraine states: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12532846.creator: Emily Stuchfield-Denby, Bruno Pereira, Damien Bouvier, Radhouane Dallel, Xavier Moisset
pmc-12532846.description: BackgroundAlthough several meta-analyses have emphasised the role of inflammation in migraine, none has accounted for the diversity of its clinical manifestations. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to provide a comprehensive and reliable assessment of cytokine levels in migraine.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed, Embase and Cochrane up to July 4–5, 2024.

pmc-12709815.title: Chromosome-level genome of Proserpinaca palustris reveals key KNOX genes related to heterophylly formation
pmc-12709815.creator: Yanjing Dong, Qian Qin, Fengqin Li, Zhonghua Tu, Chengyi Tang
pmc-12709815.description: BackgroundProserpinaca palustris, a representative heterophyllous plant, represents an emerging model for studying morphological plasticity and adaptive evolution in amphibious environments. However, the absence of a high-quality reference genome has hindered molecular investigations into its heterophylly regulation mechanisms.ResultsHere, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of P. palustris. The final assembly spans 385.

pmc-13090581.title: Smart Wound Dressings and the Biological Parameters They Monitor: A Scoping Review
pmc-13090581.creator: Sebastian Probst, Alessio Stefanelli, Sophie Groux, Natacha Bossi, Marie‐Therese Pugliese, Damien Pastor
pmc-13090581.description: Chronic wounds represent a major global health and economic burden. Smart wound dressings integrate biosensing and stimuli‐responsive materials to monitor and modulate biological parameters within the wound microenvironment. This scoping review maps the biological parameters monitored by smart wound dressings, an area not previously synthesized across preclinical and clinical contexts.

pmc-13572326.title: Dynamics of infection, vaccination and excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic among older individuals—a nationwide analysis
pmc-13572326.creator: Eva A. S. Koster, Marije H. Sluiskes, Hein Putter, Frits R. Rosendaal, Astrid van Hylckama Vlieg, Mark G. J. de Boer, Liesbeth C. de Wreede
pmc-13572326.description: The Coronavirus Diseases (COVID-19) pandemic led to excess mortality in many countries, i.e., to more deaths than expected. Older individuals generally had higher absolute risks of excess death. The complex dynamics of infection, vaccination and excess mortality have not yet been captured in one comprehensive model.

pmc-13616699.title: Predicting global horizontal irradiance using regression-based machine learning models in high-altitude environments
pmc-13616699.creator: Milton Edward Humpiri-Flores, David Mamani-Pari, Danny Lévano, Roel Dante Gomez Apaza, Esteban Tocto-Cano, Ángel Rosendo Condori-Coaquira, Javier Linkolk López-Gonzales
pmc-13616699.description: Global solar radiation is a fundamental component of the Earth's energy balance and plays a critical role in integrating renewable energy into electrical systems. However, its pronounced variability, particularly in high-altitude regions, constrains energy stability and complicates planning processes. This study evaluated regression-based and machine-learning models for 1-day-ahead prediction of global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in Juliaca, Peru (>3,800 m.a.s.l.
